title: Crossing with another’s support
literal_meaning: Crossing the Vaitarani while holding a cow’s tail.
meaning_odia: ଗୋରୁର ଲାଙ୍ଗୁଡ ଧରି ବୈତରଣୀ ପାର ହେବାର ଛବି। ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଅନୁସାରେ ନିଜେ ପାର ହେବାକୁ ଅସମର୍ଥ ଥିବା ବେଳେ ଅନ୍ୟର ସାହାରା ଧରି ଉଦ୍ଧାର ପାଇବାକୁ ଏହା ତୁଳନା କରେ।
explanation: The crossing is accomplished through something the traveller can hold onto. The inspected gloss uses the image for getting through a difficulty with another’s support when one cannot manage alone. Its emphasis is reliance on help.
usage_example: Original imagined example: An inexperienced organiser completes a demanding task with sustained guidance from a colleague. Looking back, they use the saying to acknowledge the support that carried them through.
cultural_context: The named river gives the obstacle a concrete form, and the held tail gives support a physical shape. The source explains the crossing as a simile of reliance; the image remains proverbial rather than a claim that such a crossing or religious deliverance has occurred.

witnesses.locator: Page15, fourth item beginning ଗୋରୁ ଲାଙ୍ଗୁଡ ଧରି.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026. Original river spelling ବୌତରଣୀ is explicitly corrected to public-witness ବୈତରଣୀ; uploaded ଲାଙ୍ଗୁଡ and ପାରି remain unchanged.
Public counterpart uses ଲାଙ୍ଗୁଡ଼ and the fuller ending ବୈତରଣୀ ପାର ହୋଇଯିବା. Supplies the river-name repair and explicit support/reliance gloss; not claimed as exact uploaded wording.

origin_note: Uploaded short wording has a longer public counterpart; river-name correction is documented. Earliest origin and shared lineage unknown.
